name: @marktiderman/genesis-supabase
description: Supabase for Genesis apps on web and React Native: a client with PKCE and safe defaults, Keychain session storage that survives interrupted writes, refresh only while the app is in front, native Sign in with Apple and Google, OAuth redirects, in-app account deletion, per-tenant feature switches (tenant_features), a background-job queue with schedules (genesis_jobs) on one outbox engine (/runner, shared with notifications and forms), the feature registry in the database for the feature gate (features, entitlements, flag values, feature_on), a native-to-web sign-in handoff (continue on the web, already signed in: web-handoff), and a result helper. Part of the Genesis framework.

feature.name: Account
feature.summary: Sign-in, profile and in-app account deletion, with Sign in with Apple token revocation.

steps: Enable the sign-in providers you use in Supabase Auth (email, Apple), and deploy genesis-apple-revoke if you offer Sign in with Apple.

feature.name: Tenant feature switches
feature.summary: A tenant's admins turn a shipped feature off or back on for their tenant with a reason; members hide what is off.

steps: Give tenant_features your membership rule in a migration of your own: create private.genesis_tenant_admin(tenant uuid, person uuid) returns boolean, and revoke execute on it from public, anon, authenticated (genesis-supabase README, Tenant feature switches). Without it nobody can change a switch.

feature.name: Background jobs
feature.summary: A job queue (enqueue, claim with leases, retry with backoff) and named schedules that call the app's job route with a secret.

steps: Add one job route with createJobsHandler from @marktiderman/genesis-supabase/jobs, and set GENESIS_JOBS_SECRET on the server.

For schedules: enable pg_cron and pg_net, add the Vault secrets genesis_jobs_url (the route's base URL) and genesis_jobs_secret (the same secret), then call genesis_schedule_job(name, cron, job) in a migration.

feature.name: Registry in the app's database
feature.summary: The feature registry mirrored into the database on deploy, entitlements, per-tenant flag values and SQL feature_on(), for the feature gate.

steps: Sync the registry on every deploy with the service key: syncFeatureRegistry(admin, features.json, { version: BUILD_TIME } (the build time, from a production deployment only)). Grant paid features by writing feature_entitlements from your billing webhook (a tenant's) or calling grant_person_entitlement (one person's). For person grants, define private.genesis_viewer_people(viewer) as 0016 shows.

feature.name: Continue on the web
feature.summary: A native app opens a web page signed in as the same person: a single-use, 60-second link minted by the server for the person's own account, confirmed on the page unless that browser is already signed in as them.

steps: Add two POST routes with createWebHandoff from @marktiderman/genesis-supabase/web-handoff/server (mint at /api/auth/handoff, redeem at /api/auth/redeem-handoff), using the service-role client on the server.
Add the /auth/handoff page: call takeWebHandoffFragment before analytics or error reporting load, then completeWebHandoff; send Referrer-Policy: no-referrer and frame-ancestors 'none' for it.
In the native app, call openOnWeb from @marktiderman/genesis-native/web-handoff with the mint route, the session's access token and expo-web-browser.

prefer.need: a Supabase client in the app or on the phone
prefer.why: Genesis's client sets PKCE, session storage that survives interrupted writes and refresh only while the app is in front. Server files (a service-key client) aren't checked.
